OPERATIVE REPORT

Preoperative Diagnosis: Aortic root aneurysm with severe aortic regurgitation in a patient
with a prior surgical aortic valve replacement now with prosthetic valve dysfunction.
Procedure: Redo sternotomy, aortic root replacement with a valved conduit (Bentall
procedure).

Given the patient's prior sternotomy for aortic valve replacement complicated by late
prosthetic valve dysfunction and new aortic root dilation, a redo Bentall procedure was
planned. Redo median sternotomy was performed with careful dissection given dense adhesions
from the prior operation. Cardiopulmonary bypass was established via peripheral cannulation.

The aortic root and previously implanted prosthetic valve were excised. A Konect valved
conduit was selected for aortic root replacement given the need for simultaneous valve and
root replacement, and the coronary buttons were reimplanted in standard fashion.

Tissue Implant Type: Valved conduit, bioprosthesis
Valve Type Used: Konect
Implant Size: 25

Separation from bypass was achieved without difficulty. Post-implant transesophageal
echocardiography showed the mean gradient is 9 mmHg with a dimensionless valve index of
0.55 and no significant regurgitation. This was a redo procedure given the prior surgical
valve's failure.
